jobs.title: Associate Director Operational Excellence
jobs.description:
Job Description

Join Us in Shaping the Future of Animal Health

Our company is investing $895 million in expanding our manufacturing and research & development facilities in De Soto, Kansas — the state’s largest economic development project to date.

Job Summary:

As an Associate Director Operational Excellence , you will be part of a world-class team at our Center of Excellence in the Animal Health Corridor, contributing directly to the production of veterinary products that improve animal health and welfare globally.

In this role, you would work as a Lean Practitioner/Coach and Project/Program Manager. As an internal lean practitioner and coach, you will identify, analyze, act upon, and instruct others on improvements both strategically and based on daily problems. In this position, you will lead or be involved with teams on all facets of the value stream to improve business outcomes.   You will apply lean tools, thinking, and change management methodologies as you develop colleagues at all levels so that continuous improvement is in everyone's DNA.
As a project and program manager, you will lead projects to improve supply, increase productivity/reduce cost. You will lead teams with value-scouting exercises and lead more complex projects to achieve business outcomes.

Primary Responsibilities:

- Initiate, implement, and coach improvement projects using Lean tools (Standardization, 5S, Poke Yoke, Kaizens, Value Stream Mapping, Visual Management, etc.) to create flow and work smarter to improve performance, safety, quality, delivery, and cost.
- Hands-on support for operational problems and cross-functional investigations by conducting thorough scientific problem-solving techniques.
- Coach lean roadmaps and provide training.
- Continue to develop yourself in lean, inclusion, and change management. With this knowledge, you develop colleagues at all organizational levels by leading by example during improvement initiatives and coaching sponsors and stakeholders.

Primary Responsibilities of Project/Program Manager:

- Demonstrated senior leadership behaviors

- Facilitating value scouting workshops at sites.
- Project lead on larger cost savings projects.
- Lead regional cost-saving project governance and reporting.
- Additional duties as assigned

Required Experience and Skills:

- Bachelor's degree in project management, biology, engineering, or a relevant field.
- 5-7 years of demonstrable work experience with continuous improvement in one of the following fields: biopharmaceuticals, manufacturing, or quality.
- Experience in coaching staff in incorporating continuous improvement into their departments.
- Experience in facilitating project teams and project management.
- Result-oriented and able to manage many different tasks/projects and demonstrated ability to adapt to changes in priorities.
- Proficient in working with data, making trends visible, and performing data analysis.
- Proficient with Microsoft Office (Outlook, Word, Excel, Project, etc.)
- Team player with a "go-to-the-shop-floor" attitude, analytical & eager to learn.
- A pleasant, communicative skilled personality who can connect and coach colleagues in production as well as within management. Demonstrated ability to coach and influence management and change management.
- Experience with deploying and coaching lean in multiple environments
- Demonstrated use of all commonly used lean tools and concepts.
- Experience deploying strategy (Hoshin Kanri, Policy Deployment) and A3 Thinking in multiple levels of an organization.

Preferred Experience and Skills:

- Master's degree in management or business.
- Project Management Certification
- Formal training in Lean

Required Skills:
Lean Methodologies, Manufacturing, Manufacturing Operations, Manufacturing Production, Manufacturing Productivity, Operational Excellence (OpEx), Process Efficiency Improvements, Process Improvements, Process Optimization, Process Standardization, Project Management

jobs.title: Director, Operations - Pharm Ops
jobs.description:
Job Description

At our company, we aspire to be the premier research-intensive biopharmaceutical company, using the power of leading-edge science to save and improve lives around the world. We are at the forefront of research to deliver innovative health solutions that advance the prevention and treatment of diseases in people and animals.

Join a purpose-built, agile small molecule manufacturing site where your work will help bring important medicines to patients in the U.S. This facility is designed to move quickly and reliably, receiving technology transfers from commercialization sites and fast-following into production with a focus on quality, safety, and operational excellence.

At our site, you’ll be part of a team committed to creating a safe, environmentally responsible, and compliant workplace where people can do their best work. We are building deep small molecule expertise in the U.S., and we want team members who are excited to grow their skills, help improve how we operate, and contribute to a site positioned for future growth.

Reports To:
Site Ops Lead

Job Purpose:
The Director, IPT Leader, Pharm Ops provides leadership, technical and operational expertise to the Integrated Process Team (IPT) supporting the Pharmaceutical Operations manufacturing value stream at the Elkton, VA site. This role is accountable for shaping the future operating model for our new small molecule pharmaceutical manufacturing facility, including project and site readiness, organizational design, and the establishment of operating rhythms, governance, IPT culture, Ways of Working, and performance standards.
In the early project phases, the incumbent will lead strategic and tactical planning, cross-functional coordination, and project management activities required to support successful site build-out and operational ramp-up. As the site matures, the role will transition into full IPT leadership, accountable for safe, compliant, reliable, and efficient pharmaceutical operations, delivery performance, continuous improvement, stewardship, and people development. The incumbent serves as a member of the site leadership team and ensures alignment of site priorities with divisional and company strategies.

Primary Responsibilities:

Site Leadership and Strategy
- Serve as a member of the Site Leadership Team and help align IPT priorities with site and company strategy.

- Provide direction to establish tactical and strategic plans that support Pharm Ops ramp-up and long-term operational success.

- Partner across the site and with above-site teams to ensure strong coordination, decision-making, and execution.

- Represent the IPT and the site as needed with internal stakeholders and external partners.

Future-State Operating Model and Ramp-Up
- Lead the development of the future-state operating model for Pharm Ops at Elkton, VA.

- Support site start-up, ramp-up, and operational readiness activities through project leadership and cross-functional coordination.

- Help define organizational structure, organizational culture, operating rhythms, governance, and capability needs for the evolving site.

- Ensure readiness plans, risk assessments, and implementation plans are developed and executed effectively.

Operations Excellence and Delivery
- Ensure safe, compliant, reliable, and right-first-time pharmaceutical operations in support of production and supply objectives.

- Lead operational reviews and daily management routines to maintain visibility to performance, issues, and priorities.

- Drive structured problem solving and the use of performance metrics to identify trends, action plans, and opportunities for improvement.

- Support production planning, resource deployment, and issue resolution to meet site objectives.

- Promote lean thinking and continuous improvement to improve flow, throughput, right-first-time performance, and operational stability.

Financial Stewardship
- Support and/or own budget planning and financial stewardship for the IPT, including operating and capital spend.

- Partner with site leadership to identify opportunities for productivity, efficiency, and cost improvement.

- Ensure resources are allocated effectively to support current and future business needs.

Quality and Safety Stewardship
- Promote a strong quality culture and support a state of permanent inspection readiness.

- Ensure cGMP compliance and effective management of deviations, investigations, and corrective actions.

- Partner with Quality, EHS, Engineering, Technical, and Supply Chain teams to support site priorities and maintain strong compliance standards.

- Ensure appropriate training, documentation, and change management practices are in place to support safe and compliant operations.

- Champion a strong safety culture and support risk management activities across the IPT.

People Leadership
- Lead, coach, and develop a team of leaders and contributors to build a high-performing organization.

- Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, empowerment, and continuous learning.

- Support talent development, succession planning, and ongoing skill-building within the IPT.

- Communicate clearly and regularly to align the team around priorities, expectations, and performance.

Minimum Required Education, Experience:
- Bachelor’s degree required. Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Engineering, or a related scientific/technical discipline is preferred.

- 10+ years of relevant experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology or other regulated manufacturing environments.

- Leadership experience in one or more of the following areas: Manufacturing, Technical Operations, Quality Operations, Engineering, and/or Production Planning.

- Experience leading teams with direct and indirect reports.

- Strong knowledge of cGMP, quality systems, regulatory readiness, and safety/environmental practices.

- Demonstrated experience with operational planning, project leadership, or site ramp-up/start-up activities.

- Proven ability to lead in complex environments and manage multiple priorities across functions.

- Strong business acumen and experience with financial stewardship and resource planning.

- Experience applying Lean Six Sigma, continuous improvement, and structured problem-solving tools.

At our company, we aspire to be the premier research-intensive biopharmaceutical company, using the power of leading-edge science to save and improve lives around the world. At our site, you’ll be part of a team committed to creating a safe, environmentally responsible, and compliant workplace where people can do their best work. The Director, IPT Leader, API provides leadership, technical and operational expertise to the Integrated Process Team (IPT) supporting the API manufacturing value stream at the Elkton, VA site. Onder deze afdeling valt het team Site Engineering, dat technische projecten realiseert op het gebied van nieuwbouw, renovatie en verbouwing op de locaties Boxmeer en De Bilt. Dit omvat onder meer bouwkundige, proces technische en installatieprojecten, evenals verpakkingsconcepten. Het team levert hiervoor projectmanagement- en projectengineering-support.

In deze rol ben je de single point of contact voor een aan jou toegewezen interne klant (Productie-Unit of Center of Excellence). In deze rol werk je nauw samen met een grote diversiteit aan interne (e.g. Asset Management, Facilities , Environment, Health & Safety, Manufacturing (EHS)) en externe stakeholders (leveranciers, contractors ) en rapporteer je aan de Manager Site Engineering.

Are you ready to drive operational excellence in a dynamic manufacturing environment? Join our Animal Health site in Boxmeer and lead Lean Six Sigma initiatives that improve performance, empower teams, and deliver sustainable business results.

For our animal health location in Boxmeer we are currently recruiting a: Lean Six Sigma Specialist (Manufacturing)

Welcome to our team
The production facilities in Boxmeer are part of the global Animal Health manufacturing network. We produce and package animal health products according to GMP standards. We work according to the Production System (MPS), which is based on Lean Six Sigma, continuous improvement, and inclusion principles.
The IPT Live Vaccines organisation consists of two production departments and support teams for Maintenance & Reliability and Improvement. The IPT is responsible for the preparation of live bulk vaccines, aseptic filling and freeze-drying of live attenuated vaccines. With approximately 270 FTE, IPT Live offers a dynamic environment where operational excellence, collaboration and shop floor engagement are key.

Purpose of the Role
The Lean Six Sigma Specialist plays a critical role in driving operational excellence within IPT Live by leading strategic improvement initiatives that enhance performance, efficiency, quality, and ways of working. As a highly visible presence on the shop floor, you will work closely with operational teams to identify opportunities, translate insights into sustainable improvement actions, and address complex challenges through structured problem-solving and data-driven decision-making.
In this role, you will act as a catalyst for change by coaching teams, developing Lean Six Sigma capabilities, and fostering a culture of continuous improvement. Through strong stakeholder management and cross-functional collaboration, you will bring people together around shared objectives, ensure alignment on priorities, and help deliver measurable and lasting business results. By applying Lean, Six Sigma, and MPS principles, you will support IPT Live in achieving its operational and strategic goals while continuously raising the organization's improvement maturity.

Tasks and responsibilities
- Design, implement, and continuously improve the Lean Six Sigma programme within IPT Live, ensuring alignment with MPS principles and business priorities.
- Build Lean Six Sigma capabilities across the organization by establishing standards, providing training, coaching colleagues, and leading by example.
- Maintain a strong shop floor presence to understand operational challenges, identify improvement opportunities, and translate ideas into practical and sustainable solutions.
- Lead and support cross-functional improvement projects, investigations, and problem-solving efforts using data analytics, structured root cause analysis, and effective follow-up.
- Coach sponsors, project leaders, and practitioners in the application of Lean, Six Sigma, change management, and inclusion principles.
- Engage and influence stakeholders at all levels of the organization to build alignment, ownership, and commitment around improvement priorities.
- Use performance metrics, benchmarking, and data analysis to identify, prioritize, and address operational and business improvement opportunities.
- Collaborate with peers across the network to share best practices and contribute to global MPS and continuous improvement communities.
- Support IPT Live in achieving its business objectives by initiating, leading, and actively participating in improvement initiatives and ad hoc projects.

What we ask
- Bachelor's or Master's degree, demonstrating an academic level of thinking and problem-solving.
- Proven experience in establishing, leading, or making a significant contribution to Lean Six Sigma or continuous improvement programs within a manufacturing or operational environment.
- Lean Six Sigma Black Belt certification, or Green Belt certification with substantial practical experience and the willingness and capability to obtain Black Belt certification.
- Strong analytical, facilitation, project management, and stakeholder management skills.
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills in both Dutch and English.

Working with us means contributing to animal health in an international environment alongside dedicated colleagues. You will have ample opportunities to grow, develop your skills, and make a meaningful impact. In addition, we offer an attractive benefits package, including:

Operating within the Architecture, Integration, Data Engineering & Data Enablement (AIDE) organization, this role partners closely with Value Teams, platform teams, analytics and AI teams, and enterprise governance bodies to embed data enablement capabilities into business domains.
Working in a matrixed, domain‑centric environment, the Data Enablement Lead acts as a product manager for data enablement, translating governance and platform capabilities into scalable, consumable outcomes that accelerate business value, analytics, and AI adoption.

What will you do
- Define and drive the Data Enablement strategy for assigned data domains, aligned with Value Teams, Animal Health Data Platform and One Data Program objectives.
- Establish and enforce data enablement standards, guardrails, and design principles covering data quality, metadata, lineage, access, privacy, and AI readiness.
- Act as the AIDE liaison to Value Teams, co‑designing domain data products while maintaining clear separation between enablement and ownership.
- Enable self‑service data capabilities with guardrails, in collaboration with platforms, engineering, and security teams.
- Own and evolve data enablement roadmaps, prioritizing capabilities based on domain needs, adoption, and business value.
- Ensure data products are discoverable, trusted, reusable, and fit for advanced analytics and GenAI use cases.
- Partner with analytics, AI, and data science teams to ensure data enablement supports current and future AI needs.
- Define and track product‑style metrics (adoption, data quality, time‑to‑delivery, consumer satisfaction).
- Support domain governance councils, escalation paths, and cross‑domain alignment.

- Management: Lead the design and implementation of scalable, compliant data enablement capabilities aligned with business priorities. Support leadership vision and strategy for a federated, domain‑centric data operating model.
- Process and Insight: Translate governance and platform capabilities into repeatable enablement processes. Promote data‑driven decision‑making using metrics and insights from enablement outcomes.
- Product & Delivery: Operate with a data‑as‑a‑product mindset, managing enablement backlogs, roadmaps, and lifecycle evolution. Deliver incrementally using agile ways of working.
- Relationships: Build trusted partnerships with Value Teams, platform teams, analytics teams, and enterprise governance stakeholders. Influence without assuming data ownership.

jobs.description:
Job Description

Join our fast-growing Animal Health organization and shape the learning and capability strategy that powers our ambitious transformation agenda.

For our Animal Health location Boxmeer, we are currently recruiting a Learning & Development Lead (Manufacturing)

Welcome to our team
Our Boxmeer site manufactures and packages animal health products according to Good Manufacturing Practices standards (GMP). The Learning & Development (L&D) team sits within the Center of Excellence Operational Excellence (CoE OPX) alongside the MPS and SAP Data & Processes teams. L&D drives business performance by designing, delivering and continuously improving targeted learning solutions, capability frameworks and development pathways that build skills, increase adoption and sustain operational excellence across the organization. In a fast-changing and highly regulated manufacturing environment, the role of L&D is essential in enabling transformation, supporting strategic priorities, and helping employees at all levels adapt to new ways of working.

Purpose of the role
Reporting to the Director of Operational Excellence, you play a key role in enabling performance and delivering results at our Boxmeer and De Bilt manufacturing sites. You will be responsible for shaping and ensuring the effective execution of the local learning strategy in alignment with strategic business priorities and our global L&D frameworks. You will lead and develop a team of 4 L&D professionals and act as a trusted partner to senior stakeholders, translating business needs into impactful learning and capability solutions that drive performance improvement, change adoption, and sustainable behavior change. You will work closely with Site Leaders, Global L&D, and external learning partners to ensure that L&D contributes directly to strategic objectives and workforce readiness.

Main tasks and responsibilities
·       Shape the learning and capability strategy for the site. Translate business and workforce needs into a clear learning strategy and execute solutions in partnership with business leaders, HRBPs, and site functions to ensure an integrated plan.
·       Serve as strategic learning business partner and advisor to Senior Leadership; position L&D as a lever for the Manufacturing the Future Strategy and broader business transformation.
·       Lead and manage a team of site L&D Specialists and -admins: set priorities, establish measurable outcomes, and oversee analysis, design, and execution of site learning needs.
·       Align site-level execution with Global Learning & Development (GL&D), localizing global initiatives and ensuring proper delivery of core and common curriculum.
·       Strengthen the skills and capabilities of the current and future workforce to ensure relevance, readiness, and on-time execution.
·       Run L&D like a business: drive efficiencies, align governance to business needs, and build L&D capability for higher impact.
·       Establish, deepen, and sustain relationships with site leadership, managers, and HR business partners to identify business needs, capability gaps, and priorities.
·       Lead cross-functional collaboration with stakeholders and subject-matter experts to define desired performance outcomes and design appropriate learning solutions.
·       Identify performance gaps and deliver or facilitate learning solutions; document customization and localization needs for global programs and develop local solutions when required.
·       Drive automation and digitalization within Learning & Development and training processes to streamline processes, improve learner experience, and enhance overall efficiency.
·       Own and administer the regional/site learning system (including QMS Training Subsystem standards); ensure compliance with GL&D, GMP, EHS, and other required standards.
·       Act as Business Process Owner for QMS GMP Training Standard (2.2) and serve as key contact for GMP audits and regulatory inspections.
·       Deliver training directly when needed and/or support local SMEs to develop and deliver training; manage site onboarding aligned with Manufacturing Division onboarding.
·       Act as liaison with Learning Support Services to align tools and administration with site needs; ensure solutions meet client requirements.
·       Stay current on L&D tools, techniques, strategies, and best practices; share leading practices with teams and stakeholders.
·       Monitor progress of strategic learning initiatives, remove barriers, and ensure timely delivery, adoption, and measurable impact.

Your profile
- Bachelor’s or master’s degree in a relevant field (e.g., Human Resource Management, Organizational Psychology, Business Administration, Engineering).
- Proven experience designing and executing Learning strategy.
- Strong experience with leading transformational change, stakeholder management, and navigating resistance to change.
- Strong ability to influence, build commitment, and manage competing priorities in a complex and evolving environment.
- Familiarity or affinity with regulated manufacturing environments and working within compliance frameworks.
- Proven ability to lead and mentor a small team of specialists, whether in a temporary project role or within a formal reporting structure.
- Drive for Continuous Improvement and a digital mindset with experience in automating and digitalizing (learning) processes.
- Fluent in English. Proficiency in Dutch is preferred, or a willingness to learn Dutch is highly valued.
- Ideally based within commuting distance of Boxmeer, or willing to relocate, as the role requires a strong on-site presence of at least four days per week.

What we offer
A high-impact role within a complex site of more than 2.500 colleagues, contributing to the company’s future by strengthening workforce capabilities through targeted continuous improvement and transformation programs. This is an opportunity to apply strategic planning, execution excellence, networking, and partnership skills to drive meaningful progress. You will have the chance to shape how our workforce learns, adapts, and performs in a changing environment. Our benefits are very competitive, and the summary below will give you an idea of what you can expect.
·       Competitive compensation aligned with your knowledge and experience.
·       3% year-end payment and an annual bonus based on individual and company performance.
·       35,5 days of leave.
·       Solid Pension Plan.
·       Travel allowance for commuting.
·       Numerous training, coaching and e-learning modules for long term job opportunities and development.
·       Excellent accessibility: the train station is right by our main entrance and there is ample parking.
·       High-quality company restaurant with fresh, healthy options daily.
·       Contribution toward your personal sports/fitness membership to support your vitality.
·       Beautiful private park on the premises, ideal for a walk, break, or moment of relaxation.
·       Mental well-being support via Lyra Health for you and your family members.
·       Access to a dedicated prayer/meditation room.

Animal Health
Our Animal Health Division is a trusted global leader in veterinary medicine, dedicated to preserving and improving health, well-being, and performance of animals and the people who care for them. We are a global team of professionals working together to make a positive difference in animal care and the world’s food supply and have a deep sense of responsibility towards our customers, consumers, animals, society, and our planet.
Through our commitment to The Science of Healthier Animals®, we offer veterinarians, farmers, pet owners and governments one of the widest ranges of veterinary pharmaceuticals, vaccines and health management solutions and services as well as an extensive suite of digitally connected identification, traceability and monitoring products. We invest in dynamic and comprehensive R&D resources and a modern, global supply chain. We are present in more than 50 countries, while our products are available in some 150 markets.

The Sales Manager & Strategic Account Lead is a pivotal leadership role combining people leadership, commercial execution, strategic account management, and customer engagement.
This role is responsible for building and developing a high-performing field team and for strengthening engagement across general practice, hospitals, pharmacies, and other relevant healthcare stakeholders and partners.
In parallel, the role serves as a strategic lead for Primary Care business and partnerships, with responsibility for improving patient care pathways through high-level stakeholder engagement, developing innovative partnerships, and driving customer segmentation and targeting excellence to optimize commercial execution and customer engagement.
The successful candidate will combine strong commercial capabilities with an entrepreneurial mindset, a passion for developing people, and the ability to translate strategy and customer insights into impactful execution.

Key Responsibilities:

Sales Team Leadership

- Build, lead, coach, and inspire a high-performing field team to achieve commercial objectives across hospital, general practice, pharmacy channels, and strategic partnerships.
- Set clear priorities, performance expectations, and development goals to support individual and team success.
- Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, continuous learning, innovation, and compliance.

Strategy Development and Cross-Functional Collaboration

- Partner closely with the Business Unit Lead, Marketing, and other cross-functional colleagues to shape commercial strategies and co-create solutions.
- Ensure that field execution and account management support overarching business and brand objectives.
- Act as a strategic bridge between field execution, Marketing, Market Access, Medical Affairs, Business Intelligence, Analytics, and other relevant functions.

Customer Segmentation & Targeting Excellence

- Lead the development, implementation, and continuous optimization of customer segmentation and targeting models.
- Ensure segmentation insights drive customer engagement strategies, account prioritization, resource allocation, omnichannel execution, and field force effectiveness.
- Translate customer, market, and behavioral data into actionable engagement frameworks.

Strategic Primary Care Engagement

- Strengthen engagement within Primary Care by building strategic relationships with key healthcare stakeholders and decision-makers.
- Identify opportunities to optimize and improve patient care pathways.
- Represent the organization in relevant healthcare forums and stakeholder engagements.

Partnership & Business Development

- Provide strategic direction and leadership in developing innovative commercial partnerships and new ways of engaging healthcare and non-traditional stakeholders.
- Identify and assess new opportunities and collaboration models that can improve customer engagement, patient pathways, and access to appropriate healthcare interventions.
- Support the development of scalable business cases and commercial models, including implementation coaching.

Primary Tasks:

Sales & People Management

- Build and develop a strong field organization.
- Coach and develop team members to enable both individual and team success.
- Analyze territory data, customer engagement metrics, and market dynamics to optimize resource allocation, targeting, and commercial performance.
- Continuously refine customer segmentation and targeting models to optimize call planning, account prioritization, and customer engagement.

Strategic Commercial Alignment

- Collaborate with Marketing and cross-functional partners to provide field-based insights that shape go-to-market strategies.
- Drive adoption of segmentation-driven and omnichannel engagement approaches across the field organization.
- Ensure field execution remains closely aligned with business priorities.

Strategic Account Management

- Identify, map, prioritize, and engage critical stakeholders influencing Primary Care and patient pathways.
- Build strategic relationships with relevant healthcare decision-makers at local and regional levels.
- Identify friction points and opportunities within patient pathways and collaborate on solutions to improve patient outcomes.

Business Development & Partnerships

- Further develop strategic approaches to partnerships across traditional and non-traditional healthcare stakeholders.
- Prioritize partnership opportunities based on market insights, customer needs, and business potential.
- Support implementation of partnership models and commercial initiatives.

Education

- Master’s or Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Life Sciences, Public Health, or a related field.

Experience

- Strong experience from the pharmaceutical, healthcare, or another relevant commercial environment.
- Demonstrated ability to translate strategy into impactful execution.
- Previous people leadership or Sales Manager experience is preferred but not required.
- Experience in Key Account Management, strategic account management, commercial excellence, sales force effectiveness, customer engagement, or similar commercially focused roles is an advantage.
- Experience using customer segmentation, targeting, customer insights, and analytics to improve commercial execution is preferred.

Leadership & People Development

- A people-oriented leader who can inspire, coach, and develop others.
- Ability to lead through collaboration, influence, accountability, and a genuine desire to enable others to succeed.

Market Knowledge

- Strong understanding of the Danish healthcare environment and the interaction between Primary Care, pharmacies, scientific leaders, healthcare decision-makers, and other relevant stakeholders.

Commercial & Strategic Acumen

- Strong strategic and entrepreneurial mindset.

The CSRM Physician is a leader in pharmacovigilance and is responsible for the overall clinical risk management and safety surveillance of assigned marketed products.  As chairs of the Risk Management Safety Team (RMST), CSRM physicians lead the development and maintenance of risk management and pharmacovigilance plans.

- Chair of the Risk Management and Safety Team (RMST) a subteam of the PDT, for assigned products.  This may include participation in internal and joint internal/external research project teams relevant to the further study of marketed compounds.

- Duties include all aspects of safety data evaluation, including assessing safety from multiple sources, e.g., clinical trials, literature and post-approval use and ensuring completeness of safety information in company core data sheets (CCDS).

jobs.title: Clinical Safety and Risk Management Associate Principal Scientist
jobs.description:
Job Description

The Clinical Safety and Risk Management Medical Associate Principal Scientist performs primary medical review of serious adverse experience (AE) reports and other AE reports of interest in order to monitor and describe the safety profile of assigned products.
Takes an active role in the oversight and development of pharmacovigilance and risk management plans (RMPs) of assigned products under the direction/guidance of the CSRM physician.
Assists the CSRM physician to prepare responses to inquiries from health professionals and regulatory agencies regarding adverse experiences reported for assigned products.
In collaboration with the CSRM physician, strategizes with the Risk Management Safety Team (RMST) recommending appropriate data to respond to queries and analyze data.

Primary activities include, but are not limited to:
- Applies clinical, pharmacological, and epidemiologic knowledge and information technology (IT) skills in order to manage the safety surveillance and risk management of assigned products in collaboration with the CSRM physician

- In collaboration with the CSRM physician, accountable for monitoring the overall safety profile of assigned products and for describing the safety profile to ensure external communications regarding the safety of these products are accurate

- Performs safety surveillance review of adverse experience reports for assigned products which includes reviewing individual AE reports, aggregate safety data, published literature, and information from external databases

- Works with CSRM physician to select and analyze the appropriate data from available IT systems in order to investigate safety issues

- Prepares responses to safety inquiries from health care professionals, regulatory agencies, subsidiary staff, and other internal customers

- Demonstrates a working knowledge of pharmacovigilance and risk management; may educate stakeholders outside of CSRM about risk management and the role of CSRM

- Prepares summaries and analyses of safety related data for regulatory documents such as Periodic Safety Update Reports (PSURs), Developmental Safety Update Reports (DSURs) and summaries in support of regulatory filings

- Core member of RMST; represents CSRM on cross-functional teams and committees as appropriate. Assists the RMST with the development, maintenance, and monitoring of RMPs and Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategies (REMS) for assigned products

- Participates in the development, implementation and evaluation of standards, processes, metrics, and other department initiatives.

Qualifications, Skills and Experience:
- At least two years of clinical experience in a patient care setting is required

- Minimum 5 years of professional experience with both clinical and pharmaceutical industry experience required, of which a minimum of 2 years MUST include safety experience (e.g. PV or clinical) involving causality assessment, analysis of aggregate safety data and/or authoring of safety documents.

- Experience in drug safety, pharmacovigilance and/or risk management

- Excellent writing and communication skills in English

- Demonstrated leadership skills in managing programs, processes, and facilitating meetings

- Effective presentation skills and experience influencing and negotiating

- Computer skills - use of database and basic MS Office suite applications

- Problem solving, conflict resolution and critical thinking skills

- Candidates without prior pharmaceutical industry experience are welcome to apply and may be considered for a more junior entry level.

Preferred Experience and Skills:
- Subject matter expertise in specific departmental programs, SOPS, and departmental initiatives.

Education:
- Medical Doctor (MD)
